title: Integral-operator characterization of spectral functions of real Jacobi-type five-diagonal pencils
author: Sergey M. Zagorodnyuk
work: The Inverse Spectral Problem for Jacobi-Type Pencils
source_version: Official SIGMA 13 (2017) article 085, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2017.085; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The inverse construction must recover a real symmetric five-diagonal matrix from a generally non-symmetric polynomial-domain operator, while controlling the positivity of its second subdiagonal. It simultaneously reconstructs the two initial pencil parameters and proves equality of the model operator on both the constant and positive-degree polynomial sectors. This generalized inverse spectral problem exceeds the ordinary three-term Favard correspondence.

No symmetry/self-adjointness/boundedness of A itself, unique integral measure, multiplication-operator simplification or later perturbation formula is asserted; no neighboring corollary is counted. proof_review.note: Complete3.1 necessity and sufficiency and Lemma3.2 read. Necessity uses the prior associated-polynomial integral model, proves triangular positive-leading behavior, and identifies symmetry of A times multiplication with J5. Sufficiency proves strict positivity of S from the triangular cyclic vector, constructs normalized p1 and alpha,beta from the moment Hankel determinant, takes the Favard Jacobi matrix of sigma, defines J5 through A Lambda0 on its orthogonal-polynomial basis, proves real five-diagonality and positive second subdiagonal, then identifies the reconstructed associated operator both on xP and on1. Favard and the prior associated-polynomial model are established background. No uniqueness of the integral measure, no multiplication-operator simplification, and no later special perturbation formula is asserted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Hermitian nonnegative sesquilinear S on complex polynomials. It is the spectral function of Theta=(J3,J5,alpha,beta), with J3 real Jacobi positive subdiagonal,J5 real symmetric five-diagonal positive second subdiagonal,alpha>0,beta real, iff S(u,v)=integral u(A)(1) conjugate(v(A)(1)) d sigma, for a probability measure sigma on R with all finite moments and strictly positive integral |g|^2 for every nonzero polynomial. A has exactly polynomial domain, raises x^k to degree k+1 with positive real leading coefficient and real remaining coefficients, and A Lambda0 is symmetric on polynomials. No boundedness, self-adjointness or symmetry of A itself is assumed.
